generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The Javadoc for `createClient` references `{@link SystemIndexMigrationInfo#getOrigin()}`, but the method is actually defined on `SystemResourceMigrationInfo` (the sealed parent). The link should point to `SystemResourceMigrationInfo#getOrigin()` to be accurate.

The `SystemResourceDescriptor.getOrigin()` method and the `SystemDataStreamDescriptor.origin` field can be `null` (several test call-sites pass `null`, e.g. `#ZXCTG`), yet neither the interface method nor the field carries a `@Nullable` annotation. The `SystemIndexDescriptor.getOrigin()` Javadoc also doesn't mention nullability. Since `createClient()` in `SystemResourceMigrationInfo` passes the result directly to `new OriginSettingClient(baseClient, this.getOrigin())`, a null origin could cause a subtle NPE downstream. Consider adding `@Nullable` to the interface method and documenting that the origin is optional.

The condition on this line relies on `&&` binding tighter than `||`:
```java
if (errors != null && errors.isEmpty() == false || status.exception() != null) {
```
While the precedence is correct as written, adding explicit parentheses would make the intent immediately clear and prevent a future edit from accidentally changing the logic:
```java
if ((errors != null && errors.isEmpty() == false) || status.exception() != null) {
```
